# Cypress of Cash (`cypress-of-cash`)

Daily bank reconciliation for nursing homes: bank lines with no book entry, checks that cleared for a different amount, stale outstanding checks, deposits in transit too long and the unexplained difference per account. Bank account numbers and book memos (which can name residents) are masked before results reach the model.

**Cypress never moves money or logs in to a bank.**

Evergreen ver 1 · Financial services · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`evergreen-core`](../evergreen-core)

```bash
npx -y cypress-of-cash demo
npx -y cypress-of-cash mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

A fictional Cedar Hollow operating account reconciled on 31 March 2026. Planted:

- The Medicare deposit was booked a day before the bank posted it. It still matches.
- Check 10443 cleared for 2650; the books have 2560.
- A managed care EFT and a card processing fee are on the bank statement but not in the books.
- Check 10101, a resident refund written in November, has not cleared, so it is stale.
- A private pay deposit booked 20 March is not on the bank statement.
- Check 10450 was written yesterday and is a normal outstanding check.
- After all of that, the bank is still 45 higher than the books.

The account number and the resident named in a memo are in [`phi-canaries.json`](fixtures/phi-canaries.json); they must never reach the model. [`rules-typo.json`](fixtures/rules-typo.json) misspells a setting, so the check refuses it.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `cypress_check` | Match bank lines to book entries and list what is left, with the unexplained difference. | runs |
| `cypress_write_report` | Write cypress-bank-rec.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and cypress-bank-rec.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/cypress). | runs |
| `cypress_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `cypress_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `cypress_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `cypress_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `bank_transfer` | Cypress never moves money or logs in to a bank. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `cypress_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `bank` (required) | Bank transactions under --root (BAI or CSV export): account, date, amount, check number, description |
| `books` (required) | Cash entries from the general ledger under --root: account, date, amount, check number, description |
| `rules` | Optional rules JSON: match_days, stale_days, transit_days, ending balances by account |
| `as_of` | Reconciliation date (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx cypress-of-cash inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Bank transactions (`bank`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `account` (required) | text (masked) | Account, Account Number, Bank Account, Acct, Account No |
| `date` (required) | date | Date, Posted, Post Date, Posting Date, Transaction Date, Entry Date |
| `amount` (required) | amount | Amount, Amt, Total, Balance, Net Amount, Payment Amount, Paid, Paid Amount |
| `check_no` | text | Check, Check #, Check Number, Check No, Serial, Reference |
| `description` | text | Description, Memo, Details, Payee, Narrative |

### Book cash entries (`books`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `account` (required) | text (masked) | Account, Account Number, Bank Account, Acct, Account No |
| `date` (required) | date | Date, Posted, Post Date, Posting Date, Transaction Date, Entry Date |
| `amount` (required) | amount | Amount, Amt, Total, Balance, Net Amount, Payment Amount, Paid, Paid Amount |
| `check_no` | text | Check, Check #, Check Number, Check No, Serial, Reference |
| `description` | text (masked) | Description, Memo, Details, Payee, Narrative |

## Settings file (`cypress_rules`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `match_days` | Match amounts within this many days (default 3) |
| `stale_days` | Checks older than this are stale (default 90) |
| `transit_days` | Deposits not on the bank after this many days are flagged (default 3) |
| `balances` | Ending balances by account number: {"1234": {"bank": 100, "book": 90}} |

## Memory

`cypress_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `cypress_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `recurring_item` | is shown with results. It never changes a check. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `evergreen-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cypress-of-cash": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "cypress-of-cash",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add cypress-of-cash -- npx -y cypress-of-cash mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
cypress-of-cash tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
cypress-of-cash sources               # the columns each input is read from
cypress-of-cash inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
cypress-of-cash call cypress_check '{"bank":"<bank>","books":"<books>"}'
cypress-of-cash eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
cypress-of-cash demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
